pr_title: Use a unique parcelRequire global per project
pr_body:
Fixes #4953.

This changes the global `parcelRequire` function to use a unique generated name per project. This should make it possible to have multiple parcel builds on the same page at once. It's generated by hashing the ~~projectRoot~~ package.json#name. Probably not perfect but better than nothing. 🤷 If anyone has a better idea on how to generate a unique id for a project that's stable over time let me know. 😄

issue_context.title: Change global parcelRequire in v2
issue_context.body:
# 💬 RFC

Scenario:
- Two different bundles are on one page; one compiled with Parcel 1.x, one with with Parcel 2.x.
- The code compiled with 2.x loads multiple modules.
- We receive the following:
![Screen Shot 2020-07-28 at 3 36 24 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1123335/88833748-9c391c00-d187-11ea-9683-26a62125492c.png)
- Presumably it is because there are API differences between v1 and v2 builds.

This could be solved in a few different ways (one or more may apply):
- change `parcelRequire` to `parcelRequire2` in v2
- allow users the ability to customize the name of `parcelRequire` (this was a feature of some bundlers in the past, and was useful in ensuring that when 3rd party code was included on pages it wouldn't introduce side effects via unknown globals)
- automagically change `parcelRequire` to include a hash (per parcel version? per some other criteria? this seems a bit difficult since the all produced bundles would also have their corresponding hashes changed?) 

## 🔦 Context

I'm trying to load a Parcel 1.x project with a Parcel 2.x project in the same page with each multiple modules that load async.

However, presumably this could come up in other cases as well:
- hash collision between the two builds because two assets at `node_modules/react/index.js` in two different projects could have a different package version but still the same asset id in `parcelRequire("<<id>>")`
- since this considered "internal API" (i think?) it could vary between minor versions, and cause issues similar to the one I'm seeing between 1.x and 2.x

<!--- Providing context helps us come up with a solution that is most useful in the real world -->

## 💻 Examples

See scenarios; I'm sure @mischnic and @devongovett have more 👍

review_comments: Is there some precedent (in Webpack?) for `module.bundle.root`? If not, why "root"?
AFAIK module.bundle in general is a parcel thing... I chose root here because it represents the root bundle on the page - the current parcelRequire global. Open to other names.
